questions.question: Explain how retort pouches compare with glass jars in terms of safety and durability. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how retort pouches compare with glass jars in terms of safety and
  • durability..
  • [U]/[CO1]
  • Retort pouches are flexible laminated packaging materials designed to withstand thermal
  • sterilization similar to canned foods. They provide excellent barrier properties against oxygen
  • and moisture. Compared with glass jars, retort pouches are lighter in weight, r equire less
  • storage space, and reduce transportation costs. They also heat more rapidly during
  • sterilization, improving energy efficiency. However, glass jars are more rigid and offer better
  • resistance to puncture and physical damage. Glass is chemically i nert and reusable, while
  • retort pouches are usually single use laminated materials. In terms of safety, both packaging
  • systems can effectively preserve food if properly sealed and sterilized.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the need for food packaging. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the need for food packaging?
  • [E]/[CO2]
  • Food packaging plays an essential role in maintaining food quality and safety. It protects food
  • products from physical damage, microbial contamination, moisture loss, and oxidation.
  • Packaging helps extend the shelf life of foods by providing barriers against environmental
  • factors such as oxygen, light, and humidity. It also facilitates storage, transportation, and
  • marketing of foo d products. In addition, packaging provides important information to
  • consumers, including nutritional content, ingredients, expiry date, and storage instructions.
  • Therefore, effective packaging ensures food safety, convenience, and product integrity.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of hermetic sealing in canned food products. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of hermetic sealing in canned food products.[U]/[CO5]
  • Hermetic sealing refers to airtight sealing of food containers to prevent entry of
  • microorganisms, gases, and contaminants. In canned foods, hermetic sealing is essential to
  • maintain sterility after thermal processing. It prevents recontamination of the product by
  • bacteria, yeast, or molds. A proper hermetic seal also prevents leakage and protects food from
  • oxygen exposure that may cause spoilage or oxidation. Thus, hermetic sealin g plays a crucial
  • role in ensuring safety, stability, and extended shelf life of canned food products.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the shelf-life attributes of foods packaged in glass containers. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the shelf-life attributes of foods packaged in glass containers.[K]/[CO1]
  • Glass containers provide excellent barrier properties against gase s, moisture, and
  • microorganisms. Since glass is chemically inert, it does not react with food components or
  • alter flavor and aroma. It also prevents oxygen penetration, which helps reduce oxidative
  • spoilage. Additionally, glass protects food from contamina tion and maintains product
  • integrity. However, exposure to light through clear glass may affect light sensitive foods;
  • therefore, colored glass containers are sometimes used. These properties help maintain the
  • quality and extend the shelf life of packaged foods.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the role of retort pouches in extending the shelf life of food products. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of retort pouches in extending the shelf life of food
  • products.[U]/[CO5]
  • Retort pouches are multilayer laminated packaging materials used for thermally processed
  • foods. They allow sterilization of packaged food at high tempera tures similar to canning. The
  • multilayer structure provides excellent barriers to oxygen, moisture, and light, which helps
  • prevent microbial growth and oxidation. Retort pouches are lightweight and provide efficient
  • heat transfer during sterilization, ensu ring effective destruction of microorganisms. As a
  • result, foods packaged in retort pouches can be stored for long periods at room temperature
  • without spoilage.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a note on thickness testing of metal sheets used in cans. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on thickness testing of metal sheets used in cans.[U]/[CO2]
  • Thickness testing is an important quality control measure in the production of metal cans.
  • The thickness of metal sheets affects the strength, durability, and corrosion resistance of the
  • can. Measurement is commonly performed using instruments such as micrometers or
  • thickness gauges. Consistent thickness ensures proper sealing, resistance to pressure during
  • processing, and prevention of leakage or structural failure. Accurate thickness testing helps
  • maintain quality standards in can manufacturing.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define edible films and explain their importance in food packaging. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define edible films and explain their importance in food packaging..[U]/[CO1]
  • Edible films are thin layers of edible materials applied to food surfaces to act as protective
  • barriers. They are usually made from proteins, polysaccharides, or lipids. Edible films help
  • reduce moisture loss, oxygen exposure, and microbial contamination. They also improve food
  • quality, extend shelf life, and reduce the use of synthetic plastic packaging. Since they are
  • biodegradable and consumable, edible films are considered environmentally frie ndly
  • alternatives in food packaging.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

• Discuss the solubility tests used for identifying common plastics.[U]/[CO5]
  • Solubility testing is used to identify plastic materials based on their ability to dissolve in
  • specific solvents. Different plastics exhibi t characteristic solubility behavior. For example,
  • polystyrene dissolves in aromatic solvents such as benzene or toluene, while polyethylene
  • and polypropylene are generally insoluble in most solvents at room temperature. By
  • observing dissolution or swellin g of the plastic sample in various solvents, it is possible to
  • determine the type of plastic used in packaging materials.

questions.question: Explain the demerits of plastics in food packaging. Discuss environmental concerns, food safety issues, and limitations in certain applications. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the demerits of plastics in food packaging.[U]/[CO1]
  • Plastics are widely used in food packaging due to their flexibility and low cost; however, they
  • have several disadvantages.
  • Environmental Concerns: Plastic waste is non biodegradabl e and accumulates in the
  • environment, causing pollution and harm to wildlife.
  • Food Safety Issues: Certain plastic additives such as plasticizers, stabilizers, and monomers
  • may migrate into food products, potentially affecting human health.
  • Limited Heat Res istance: Many plastics cannot withstand high temperatures, making them
  • unsuitable for certain sterilization processes.
  • Gas Permeability: Some plastics allow passage of oxygen and moisture, which may reduce
  • shelf life of sensitive foods.
  • Recycling Challenge s: Mixed plastic materials and multilayer packaging are difficult to
  • recycle, contributing to environmental waste problems.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define primary, secondary and tertiary packaging and explain with examples. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define primary, secondary and tertiary packaging with examples.[K]/[CO1]
  • Primary Packaging: Primary packaging is the material th at directly comes in contact with
  • the food product. Example: Milk bottles, plastic pouches, beverage cans.
  • Secondary Packaging: Secondary packaging groups multiple primary packages together for
  • protection and handling. Example: Cardboard boxes containing several food packets.
  • Tertiary Packaging: Tertiary packaging is used for bulk handling, transportation, and
  • distribution of packaged products. Example: Pallets, shrink wrapped cartons used during
  • shipping.
